description: Author-reviewed, concise intentions for populated teaching sections. Specification reference tables are deliberately excluded.

number-intro: Explain what a number represents and express a quantity in more than one way.
number-introduction-practice: Represent a number in two different ways and explain why the representations are equivalent.
number-systems-intro: Classify numbers as natural, integer, rational, irrational or real, and explain the relationships between these sets.
number-systems-practice: Classify given numbers and justify each classification.
arithmetic-intro: Explain the four operations and apply the order of operations accurately.
arithmetic-practice: Evaluate numerical expressions using a clear order of operations and justify each step.
factors-intro: Distinguish factors, multiples and prime numbers, and use prime factorisation.
factors-multiples-primes-practice: Find a prime factorisation and use it to analyse a whole number.
fractions-intro: Interpret fractions as quantities, quotients and comparisons, and recognise equivalent fractions.
fractions-practice: Calculate with fractions using equivalent forms and explain the result.
decimals-intro: Explain decimal place value and connect fractions, decimals and percentages.
decimals-percentages-practice: Calculate a percentage of a quantity using a method you can explain.
ratio-intro: Interpret ratios as multiplicative comparisons and identify equivalent ratios.
ratio-proportion-practice: Divide a quantity in a given ratio and check that the parts total the original quantity.
indices-intro: Interpret indices as powers and roots as inverse operations in appropriate number sets.
indices-roots-practice: Use an index law to simplify a product of powers and justify the rule used.
accuracy-intro: Choose an appropriate degree of accuracy and express large or small numbers in standard form.
accuracy-standard-form-practice: Write a number in standard form and explain its place value.
financial-intro: Use percentages and proportional reasoning to compare prices, discounts and financial quantities.
financial-mathematics-practice: Calculate a discounted price and explain the saving.
number-patterns-intro: Describe a numerical pattern, identify its rule and predict subsequent terms.
number-patterns-practice: Extend a sequence and explain why the proposed rule fits the known terms.
algebra-patterns-intro: Represent patterns with variables and use algebra to express a general rule.
algebra-patterns-practice: Find a formula for a growing pattern and test it against known stages.
algebra-substitution-intro: Substitute values into an algebraic expression while respecting grouping and order of operations.
algebra-substitution-practice: Evaluate expressions correctly for given values, including negative inputs.
algebra-simplifying-intro: Identify like terms and simplify expressions by collecting their coefficients.
algebra-simplifying-practice: Collect like terms and check that the simplified expression is equivalent.
algebra-factorisation-intro: Explain factorisation as writing an expression as a product and reversing expansion.
algebra-factorisation-practice: Factorise using a common factor and verify by expanding.
algebra-division-intro: Simplify algebraic fractions by cancelling factors and state any excluded values.
algebra-division-fractions-practice: Simplify an algebraic quotient and explain why its restrictions matter.
algebra-equations-intro: Solve equations using operations that preserve equality and interpret inequalities.
algebra-equations-inequalities-practice: Solve a linear equation and check the solution by substitution.
algebra-changing-intro: Rearrange a formula to make a chosen variable the subject.
algebra-changing-subject-practice: Change the subject of a formula and check the rearrangement.
algebra-words: Distinguish variables, coefficients, constants and terms, and explain what each represents.
variables-geometric-models: Represent measurements using variables and relate symbols to lengths or areas.
algebra-vocabulary-definitions: Identify and name the components of an algebraic expression accurately.
algebra-context-and-assessment: Build and interpret an algebraic model for a practical situation.
algebra-vocabulary-reflection: Predict a result, investigate it and check your mathematical explanation.
algebra-operation-words: Use sum, difference, product, quotient and fraction precisely when describing expressions.
algebra-language-practice: Translate between verbal descriptions and algebraic expressions.
expanding-principle: Explain distribution of multiplication over a grouped sum or difference.
expanding-monomial-bracket: Expand a product of one term and a bracket and account for every term.
expanding-two-brackets: Expand two brackets by applying the distributive law twice.
expanding-distribution: Identify all partial products and explain why none may be omitted.
expanding-foil-lab: Use a visual model to investigate the four products in two binomial factors.
expanding-cross-products: Collect cross-products as like terms using a clear written layout.
expanding-place-value: Multiply polynomials using a place-value layout and correctly combine terms.
expanding-homework: Apply expansion independently and check answers with an alternative representation.
expanding-scaling: Investigate how scaling a factor changes the product and justify the relationship.
expanding-zero-placeholders: Explain why zero coefficients can be useful placeholders in polynomial multiplication.
expanding-language: Explain expansions accurately using the language of groups, terms, products and distribution.
expanding-hidden-maths: Identify general patterns arising from expanded products.
expanding-beyond-school: Explore the expansion of higher-degree polynomials using the same underlying principles.
trig-intro: Identify the sides of a right-angled triangle relative to an angle and select an appropriate ratio.
trig-nine-families: Recognise the main families of right-triangle questions and choose an efficient strategy.
trig-proportion-and-limits: Explain how trigonometric ratios represent proportional relationships and investigate their behaviour.
trig-cosine-rule: Apply the cosine rule to calculate a missing side or angle in a non-right triangle.
sequences-formula-guide: Identify and interpret the formulas used for arithmetic and geometric sequences.
sequences-cicadas: Model repeating events and explain when cycles coincide.
sequences-intro: Recognise a sequence, describe its pattern and distinguish arithmetic from geometric change.
sequences-three-terms: Find a missing middle term and justify a relationship between three consecutive terms.
sequences-sum: Derive and use the arithmetic-series sum formula by pairing terms.
sequences-exam-practice: Select appropriate sequence formulas and explain solutions to examination questions.
sequences-quadratic: Recognise a quadratic sequence from its differences and investigate a general rule.
sequences-geometric: Model repeated multiplication using a geometric sequence and calculate its terms.
sequences-assessment: Explain the strategy used for a sequence problem and reflect on accuracy and efficiency.
functions-intro: Interpret points in a data set, describe the relationship between two quantities and question a fitted model.
probability-fcp: Use the fundamental counting principle to count outcomes in successive choices.
complex-intro: Explain why complex numbers extend the real numbers and interpret their basic notation.
complex-reading: Locate mathematical references and compare explanations of complex-number ideas.
ty-programme-introduction: Represent a real situation mathematically, test assumptions and explain limits of a model.
